messages:
amy_sales: Quick sync: Acme Financial wants BYOK with HSM-backed KEKs, monthly rotation, and proof we never see plaintext keys. Also asking how this changes hosted pricing. Need a one-pager + POC runbook to send by EOD.

ravi_se: Clarify whether they want the KEK kept in their KMS (we call Encrypt/Decrypt) or require an external HSM where keys never leave their hardware.

amy_sales: They prefer keys in their cloud KMS (AWS CloudHSM) and an on-prem HSM for DR. No plaintext KEKs to Redwood.

jordan_security: From security: we must confirm FIPS level, attestation reports, rotation logging, support for key import vs KMS-managed, and provide sample audit entries. We should state we only store encrypted DEKs and key IDs.

mike_eng: Implementation: we support envelope encryption. Customer wraps DEKs in their KMS and we store dek.ciphertext + payload. For AWS we support CMK in custom key store or imported key material. On-prem HSM can be proxied via KMIP or a TLS mTLS endpoint.

mike_eng: Example flow snippet: generate DEK -> aws kms encrypt --key-id <ARN> --plaintext dek.bin --ciphertext-blob dek.enc -> send dek.enc + payload to Redwood.

ravi_se: Rotation: customer rotates CMK; we retain wrapped DEKs. Unwrap should succeed via KMS using allowed key versions; we'll run compatibility check during POC.

jordan_security: Include audit sample: {"event":"kms.unwrap","key_id":"arn:..","requester":"redwood-proxy","ts":"2025-09-10T14:22:03Z","req":"r-42"}. Offer log export to customer's S3/SIEM.

laura_pm: Pricing: if key remains in customer's KMS, customer pays KMS/HSM charges; Redwood adds per-request proxy surcharge. If Redwood must provision a dedicated custom key store/HSM, add fixed infra + usage. I'll draft two pricing options.

amy_sales: POC runbook please: steps + timeline 2-3 weeks, infra checklist, what we need from Acme (KMS admin, ARNs, network).

mike_eng: Runbook sketch: 1) Kickoff (day 0) confirm KMS/HSM. 2) Network (day 1-3) setup PrivateLink/VPC peering or KMIP tunnel. 3) Key provisioning (day 3-5): grant Encrypt/Decrypt to redwood-proxy role. 4) Integration tests (day 5-8): generate/wrap/unpack sample payloads. 5) Load test (day 9-12): measure latency with wrap/unwrap. 6) Security validation (day 13-15): rotation test + attestation review.

mike_eng: Minimal IAM policy sample (customer to attach to CMK): {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::REDCORP:role/redwood-proxy"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"*"}.

ravi_se: Notes: for latency-sensitive flows recommend short TTL DEK caching or async wrapping. Document tradeoffs.

deploy-bot: infra: created acme-kmip-proxy-test (id: kmip-45) at 2025-09-11T09:01:12Z :white_check_mark:.

amy_sales: Great — please turn this into a one-pager + security Q answers, Laura will add pricing and legal flags for key escrow/breach notification. I'll send to Acme EOD. :pray:
